comparison: Both address Cys-130's role in membrane association (C2, C3, C32-C35, C42-C44). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by pharmacological and genetic evidence, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging Cys-130's role but noting 'evidence for S-acylation at Cys-130 is largely indirect' and stating 'further work will be needed to clarify the details of the mechanism.'

Both evaluate hydrophobic residues and their role in Golgi recruitment (C4, C31, C45-C46, C64-C65). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not challenge the mutagenesis data, and the editor's acceptance of Cys-130's role implicitly includes these supporting residues.

Both address minimal construct experiments showing requirement for multiple membrane-binding elements (C27-C29, C47-C50, C112). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge that polybasic region alone is insufficient, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of the systematic construct analysis.

Both evaluate truncation analysis showing differential domain contributions (C51-C57). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings, which serve as supporting data for membrane-binding determinants.

Both address ZDHHC overexpression experiments (C58-C65, with overlap on C58-C63). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on comprehensive experimental evidence. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, with editor stating the paper 'provides convincing evidence that S-acylation plays a key role,' implicitly accepting ZDHHC enzyme data.

Both evaluate PB region mutants and differential ZDHHC sensitivity (C66-C68). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings showing PB-independent membrane interaction mechanisms.

Both address endogenous NLRP3 localization in THP-1 cells (C69-C71). OpenEval also includes ZDHHC3 effects (C72-C74). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the endogenous data as consistent with overexpression findings.

Both evaluate PEG-switch assay evidence for S-acylation (C75-C83). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED despite noting interpretation uncertainty. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'evidence for S-acylation at Cys-130 is largely indirect' and citing complexity from doubly S-acylated species in C130S mutant.

Both address dynamic S-acylation cycle evidence from PalmostatinB and APT2 experiments (C84-C93). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the evidence for dynamic cycling, consistent with editor's statement about S-acylation's key role.

OpenEval R10 addresses FRAP experiments showing NLRP3 immobilization (C93-C97). Peer R3 addresses broader mechanistic claims about nigericin-induced immobilization and Golgi disruption (C5-C6, C94-C108). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'the process by which nigericin enhances membrane association is not yet fully understood.'

OpenEval R11 addresses APT2-NLRP3 segregation after nigericin (C5, C99-C101). Peer R3 includes this (C100-C101) within broader mechanistic uncertainty. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN regarding the mechanistic link between observations and proposed thioesterase segregation.

OpenEval R12 addresses Golgi disorganization and trafficking defects (C6, C102-C107). Peer R3 includes these claims (C102-C108) in broader mechanistic evaluation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN about the mechanistic connection to NLRP3 immobilization despite acknowledging the observations.

OpenEval R13 addresses mechanistic interpretation linking Golgi disruption to NLRP3 immobilization (C7, C108). Peer R3 includes C108 in broader mechanistic uncertainty. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by convergent evidence; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN about the mechanistic process.

Both evaluate monensin control experiments (C109-C111). Both find claims SUPPORTED. This control demonstrates Golgi recruitment is necessary but not sufficient for activation, and peer reviewers do not challenge these findings.

Both address the mechanistic model for membrane-binding determinants (C112-C115). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the model as consistent with experimental data showing all three elements are required.

Both address nigericin-induced NLRP3 recruitment and its dependencies (C37-C41). Both find claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept these observations as part of the convincing evidence for S-acylation's role in nigericin response.

OpenEval R16 addresses speculation about LRR domain enhancing avidity through oligomerization (C116). Rated UNCERTAIN by OpenEval as hypothesis not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R17 addresses independent validation from Yu et al. 2023 preprint (C117). Rated SUPPORTED as appropriately cited work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R18 addresses speculation about endosomal recruitment (C118). Rated UNCERTAIN as hypothesis requiring additional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R19 addresses speculation about S-acylation cycle and oligomerization thresholds (C119-C120). Rated UNCERTAIN as plausible but not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R20 addresses interpretation of prior work on mouse vs human systems (C121-C125). Rated SUPPORTED based on appropriate citation and interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R21 addresses background information from prior literature (C1, C8-C26, C33, C36, C38, C98). Rated SUPPORTED as appropriately cited context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background material.
